summary: Validate incoming data and encode outgoing data from shared schemas that also define TypeScript types.
description: Use one Effect Schema definition for runtime decoding, encoded output and the corresponding TypeScript type. Apply it where data crosses a trust boundary, such as requests, configuration or third-party responses. The guidance covers branded identifiers, tagged errors and JSON Schema for tools, with round-trip tests. Keep framework-required validators and adopt this at owned boundaries incrementally.
seoDescription: Effect Schema conventions for runtime validation and TypeScript types at request, configuration, storage and third-party data boundaries.

projectExamples.title: Validated import endpoint
projectExamples.description: Define the incoming record schema and reject malformed imports before they reach a service. Implement the import behavior and any storage separately.

projectExamples.title: Typed CLI settings file
projectExamples.description: Decode optional configuration through a closed schema and derive its TypeScript type. Keep command errors aligned with the base output contract.

plain.whatItIs: Checks data entering the app, such as requests and settings, against one written shape that the code also uses for its types.
goodAt: Rejecting badly formed input from users, outside services and settings
Keeping the data shape and the code's types from drifting apart
Testing that data converts to and from its stored form without loss
notGoodAt: Replacing checks a framework requires; keep those where the framework needs them.
